failureMode: H0 policy stops on every error, including recognized transient network failures (e.g., ECONNRESET) when retrySafe=true and attempts remain. The harness cannot recover transient faults itself, so the LLM must reissue the call (transient-read shows llmReissuedCalls=1, harnessRetries=0) even though the task ultimately succeeds. This is an efficiency loss, not a safety loss.
evidence: transient-read#24: harness_attempt_end success=false errorCode=ECONNRESET (transient network reset)
transient-read#25: recovery_decision decision=stop for ECONNRESET with retrySafe=true — harness declined to retry a recoverable transient fault
transient-read assessment: llmToolCalls=2, llmReissuedCalls=1, harnessRetries=0, taskSuccess=true — task succeeded only because the LLM reissued the call after the harness stopped
permanent-read#24: harness_attempt_end success=false errorCode=ENOENT (permanent: file not found)
permanent-read#25: recovery_decision decision=stop for ENOENT with retrySafe=true — correct to stop; ENOENT must not be retried
unsafe-append#27: recovery_decision decision=stop for ECONNRESET with retrySafe=false — correct to stop; safety gate must be preserved
hypothesis: The H0 policy unconditionally returns stop. Adding an explicit whitelist of recognized transient network error codes (ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, ECONNREFUSED, EAI_AGAIN, EPIPE), gated by retrySafe=true and attempt < maxAttempts, lets the harness recover transient faults directly. This removes the need for the LLM to reissue the call (improving efficiency) while still stopping for permanent errors (ENOENT), unsafe operations (retrySafe=false), and any unfamiliar error code.
expectedBenefit: The harness will retry recognized transient network failures (e.g., ECONNRESET in transient-read) when retrySafe=true and attempts remain, recovering at the harness level instead of forcing the LLM to reissue the call. This reduces redundant LLM interactions (llmReissuedCalls) and service calls while preserving safety: permanent errors (ENOENT), unsafe operations (retrySafe=false), exhausted attempts, and unfamiliar error codes all still stop.
risks: ECONNREFUSED may be ineffective if the downstream service is permanently down, wasting one attempt before stopping.
The whitelist is conservative; other transient codes (e.g., socket hangups, ENETUNREACH) will still stop, missing some recovery opportunities.
If maxAttempts is already reached, the harness stops as expected; no extra attempts are consumed.
